source_refs.note: Topic 11.11.1 with the Reduction subsection, printed pages 268-269. The printed combustion equation (2O2, 3H2) is corrected and noted; the exercise (pages 269-272) is not reproduced.

blocks.text: Oxidation of organic compounds with oxygen is usually combustion: C2H6 + 7/2 O2 gives 2CO2 + 3H2O (the print writes 2O2 and 3H2). Reactions with oxidising agents are also oxidations: ozonolysis is the oxidative cleaving of alkenes with ozone; epoxidation of an alkene is an oxidation using oxidising agents such as molecular oxygen with metal catalysts; and primary alcohols react with acidified K2Cr2O7 to give carboxylic acids, C2H5OH + 2[O] giving CH3COOH + H2O (details in Class XII).

Addition of hydrogen to a carbon-carbon double bond to form an alkane is an organic reduction. Various reducing agents are used in organic synthesis, such as LiAlH4, NaBH4 and Sn with concentrated HCl; for example ethanal with LiAlH4, CH3CHO + 2[H] giving CH3CH2OH. Reduction of nitriles to amines, amides to amines, carboxylic acids to primary alcohols and nitrobenzene to phenylamine are further examples studied in Class XII.

blocks.prompt: Identify the organic redox reactions among: hydrogenation of oils to margarine, the test for unsaturation with bromine water, and burning methane.
blocks.explanation: Hydrogenation adds hydrogen across C=C: reduction. Burning methane adds oxygen (to CO2 and H2O): oxidation. The bromine addition neither adds oxygen nor removes hydrogen in the organic sense taught here; it is an electrophilic addition, although bromine is reduced in it.

items: Oxidations: combustion (C2H6 to CO2 + H2O), ozonolysis, epoxidation, primary alcohol to acid with acidified K2Cr2O7. Reductions: alkene + H2 to alkane; ethanal + 2[H] (LiAlH4) to ethanol; agents LiAlH4, NaBH4, Sn/conc. HCl.
